adopted.feature: statusLine payload: fast_mode, context_window_size, cost line churn, pr.url via OSC 8
adopted.note: PASS 4 (2026-07-29) removed exceeds_200k_tokens entirely: it rendered as a bare "+" on the window size ("of 1M+"), unreadable without knowing the rule, and it signals long-context premium PRICING -- the same reason cost.total_cost_usd is omitted (DISABLE_COST_WARNINGS=1). Also stripped the "(1M context)" suffix from model.display_name so the window is stated once, not twice; renamed the pacing marker from "fast" (which collided with the fast_mode segment) to an explicit multiple, "2.2x pace"; switched burn_rate to tenths-of-a-percent precision because whole percent reported 4.5x for a true 5.4x; and made the context bar 5 cells of thin rules (━/─) instead of 8 of block shading, with rounded rather than floored cell counts so 18% is not a visually empty bar. PASS 3 (2026-07-29) added rate_limits.*.resets_at, a burn-rate pacing signal, an 8-cell context bar, ANSI threshold colours, and statusLine.refreshInterval=60. Pace = used% vs elapsed% of the window; green <=125, yellow <=175, red above, suppressed under 15% used, with absolute overrides at 75/90. A 'fast' word appears only past the warn band. Renders in ~50ms. PASS 2 note follows -- second pass after auditing all ~40 documented payload fields against the 12 in use. fast_mode matters because Opus 5 fast mode is $10/$50 per Mtok and the state drifts (2.1.219 fixed stale fast-mode on Remote Control). context_window_size disambiguates ctx% -- a fallbackModel hop to Haiku silently drops 1M to 200k, previously invisible. exceeds_200k_tokens folded into the size as a trailing '+' (long-context premium marker) instead of its own segment. Line churn uses the up/down arrow notation from rules/status-marks.md. PR label wrapped in OSC 8 with plain text inside per the linked-labels rule. Dropped the standalone 'think' segment: alwaysThinkingEnabled makes it near-constant

teej-skills marketplace.json plugin entry switched from directory source "./" to {source:command, command:'echo "$HOME/.claude/teej-skills"', mode:link}. Cache entry now links to the working tree instead of copying it, so skill edits apply next session with no version bump / plugin update / restart. Verified with `claude plugin validate`: mode is command-source-only (directory+mode fails validation), and mode:bogus / a missing command key both fail. macOS-only (link unsupported on Windows). Changing the command string itself still needs an explicit plugin update. .claude/CLAUDE.md updated to drop the old reinstall dance.

2.1.229 stopped auto-approving --force/--amend/--no-verify in /commit-push-pr, but the user-level `Bash(git:*)` allow is broader than what upstream tightened, so that default could not reach this config; branch_protection.sh only covers git commit|add on protected branches. Added a PreToolUse hook instead of permissions.deny entries because deny patterns are prefix globs and miss `git push origin foo --force` and `git -C /path push --force`. Token-walking, quote-aware (reuses the jj guard's segmentation). Blocks push --force/-f/--force-with-lease/--force-if-includes, push --no-verify, commit --amend, commit -n/--no-verify, reset --hard, gh pr merge --admin. Deliberately does NOT block `git clean -f`, `git branch -f`, `git tag -f`, `git checkout -f`, or `git push -n` (--dry-run). reset --hard is beyond the changelog line, added per rules/version-control.md. 42-case regression test in hooks/git_dangerous_flags.test.sh. pr-safety.md notes the enforcement. permissions.ask left untouched per the 2026-07-29 decline.

2.1.233 removed TodoWrite/TaskCreate/TaskGet/TaskUpdate/TaskList on Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5, Fable 5, Mythos 5 and newer. Env parser is qe.bool() so "1" coerces. VERIFIED: tools appeared mid-session from settings.json env with no restart. Background sessions and Claude Code on the web keep the tools on every model regardless

fires when a turn ends on an API error; matchers are error types (rate_limit, overloaded, authentication_failed, oauth_org_not_allowed, billing_error, invalid_request, model_not_found, server_error, max_output_tokens, unknown). Wired with matcher "" to catch all. Closes a gap for the unattended posture (CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG=1, headless mac mini): the docs do not state that Stop also fires on the error path, so a session dying on rate_limit would otherwise be silent. StopFailure discards output and exit code EXCEPT terminalSequence, so the hook emits an OSC 777 escape (ESC ]777;notify;<title>;<body> BEL) which ghostty renders as a desktop notification (desktop-notifications defaults to true). The payload field carrying the error type is undocumented, so the script scans the payload for any string matching the known enum rather than guessing a key. 9-case regression test in hooks/stop-failure-notify.test.sh

adopted.feature: retire claude-notify.sh; native notifications via preferredNotifChannel
adopted.note: REMOVED the Notification and Stop hooks and deleted hooks/claude-notify.sh, plus the CLAUDE_NOTIFY_SOUND env var that only that script read. preferredNotifChannel is already "ghostty" and the native channel raises a desktop notification for permission prompts and task completion -- exactly what the custom hook duplicated. The script shelled out to ~/Applications/claude-notify.app, an untracked machine-local binary from March that is NOT in dotfiles/, so on any other machine `test -x` failed and the hook exited 0 silently, i.e. notifications vanished with no error. Only StopFailure is not covered by the native channel, and it now has a purpose-built emitter. Channel enum: auto|terminal_bell|iterm2|iterm2_with_bell|kitty|ghostty|notifications_disabled; "auto" already desktop-notifies in iTerm2/Ghostty/Kitty

adopted.feature: move `make validate` from per-edit hook to commit time
adopted.note: DELETED ~/.claude/.claude/settings.json, whose project-scope PostToolUse hook (matcher Write|Edit|MultiEdit) ran `make -C ~/.claude pre-commit` on EVERY file edit. That target is `@$(MAKE) validate`, i.e. the whole suite -- formatting, ruff, ty, stylua, luacheck, hook tests -- over the whole repo, per edit. The matcher also named MultiEdit, a tool that no longer exists. Root cause of the hook: jj has no hook system and does not run git's hooks even in a colocated repo, so .git/hooks/pre-commit never fires on `jj describe`/`jj commit`, and the per-edit hook was compensating. Fixed at the right layer instead: skills/committing-changes step 3 now states validation is mandatory on the jj path and names `make validate` as this repo's gate. Also recorded there that `jj fix` is NOT a substitute -- it pipes file content through a tool and keeps what comes back, so it carries formatters (ruff format, stylua) but never report-only checks (ruff check, ty, luacheck, hook tests)

deferred.reason: declined 2026-08-10; left unset so the dynamic per-message default applies. The default keys off permission-mode CLASS, and auto/acceptEdits/dontAsk all count as prompting -- so with permissions.defaultMode=auto, everyday sessions already deliver peer messages with zero friction. The hold only fires in bypassPermissions sessions (which skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt:true means Teej does run), and there the approval dialog is the ONLY remaining gate, since a bypass session has no permission prompts left to catch what the message asks for. A user-scope "accept" would remove that gate globally to buy convenience in the minority case. Enum: accept|hold|refuse, ordered accept<hold<refuse; project/local settings may only tighten. NOTE the -p gap: a headless worker cannot render the approval dialog, so a held message stays held forever there -- fix per-invocation with `claude -p --settings '{"crossSessionInbound":"accept"}'`, never at user scope
